report:
# Regulatory Mechanisms of Outer Membrane Lipid Homeostasis in *Escherichia coli*: The Role of PbgA (YejM)

## Key Findings
The inner membrane protein PbgA (YejM) functions as a critical regulatory component of outer membrane lipid homeostasis by acting as an "anti-adaptor" that controls the stability of the key lipopolysaccharide (LPS) synthesis enzyme, LpxC. YejM senses the concentration of LPS in the periplasm and, in response to specific conditions, interacts with the adaptor protein LapB to sequester it. This sequestration prevents the FtsH-LapB protease complex from degrading LpxC, thereby maintaining appropriate LPS levels necessary for outer membrane integrity [Regulatory mechanisms of lipopolysaccharide synthesis in - Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32277-1). The interaction with LpxC is indirect, mediated entirely through the regulation of the FtsH protease activity.

## Function of PbgA (YejM) in Outer Membrane Lipid Homeostasis

PbgA (YejM) is an essential inner membrane protein in *Escherichia coli* whose primary function is to modulate the rate of LPS synthesis by controlling the protein levels of LpxC [An Essential Membrane Protein Modulates the Proteolysis of ...](https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/mbio.00939-20).

### LPS Sensing and Regulatory Role
LPS is a vital glycolipid that forms the protective barrier of the outer membrane (OM) [Regulatory mechanisms of lipopolysaccharide synthesis in - Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32277-1). The synthesis of LPS is tightly regulated because insufficient LPS compromises OM integrity, while excessive LPS accumulation can be toxic [Regulatory mechanisms of lipopolysaccharide synthesis in - Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32277-1).

YejM serves as a sensor for these levels. Structural data indicates that the periplasmic domain of YejM acts as a scaffold that engages lipid A, allowing the protein to sense the concentration of LPS in the periplasm [Crystal Structure of Periplasmic Domain of YejM from ...](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13125744/).
